audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer put Fizz on all seven rows of the level chart while the packet chart and content win[] both read Neeko on all seven — and every full-layer why underneath those Fizz rows described Neeko winning the stage ("Q-poke the last-hits", "E completes the kill pattern", "Pop Blossom online", "Late Neeko is an ambush"). Seven rows arguing with themselves.
audit.why: Fizz is melee with a 550-range Urchin Strike as his only approach; Neeko roots at 1000 and blooms at 800. Both other sources agree, and the full layer's own prose agrees; only the side token said otherwise.
audit.corrected: All seven sides moved to Neeko, with each why rewritten from the template into a Fizz-specific reason for that verdict.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes was the generic Level 3 / level 6 / Luden's line and said nothing about Fizz.
audit.why: The real spike story is that level 6 lets Pop Blossom pre-stun the Chum the Waters all-in, and items change the duel very little because his threat is roaming.
audit.corrected: Level 3 root-bloom is the kill pattern; level 6 pre-stuns his shark; his items change little.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns held no digit at all (defect item 3), and the two flagged interactions were never stated: Chum the Waters grounds (which is what actually denies Pop Blossom), and Seastone Trident is an attack-reset wind-up.
audit.why: From the kits: Playful/Trickster is 16/14/12/10/8 at 400 range and is untargetable during the hop — the recovery is not. Urchin Strike is 8/7.5/7/6.5/6 at 550, his only entry. Chum the Waters is 120/100/80 at 1300 range and carries grounding plus a knockup, so it, not the E hop, is the thing that denies your leap. Seastone Trident is 7/6/5/4/3 and empowers his next attack.
audit.corrected: Bait the 16s hop and burst the landing; root him out of the 550-range Urchin Strike; hold R until Chum the Waters is thrown, because it grounds.
sources: enemyKit Q/W/E/R cooldowns, ranges and flags

audit.whatIsWrong: The field said "count it out loud if you must" without ever naming a number.
audit.why: Playful/Trickster at 16s rank 1 falling to 8s maxed is the punishable window; it halves across the game, which changes how often you get a clean commit.
audit.corrected: Numbers added for Playful/Trickster, Urchin Strike and Chum the Waters.

audit.whatIsWrong: Copy-paste bleed (defect item 2): dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim, dontsFull[1].d was the generic clone paragraph under a river-shoving title, dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim. tldr also claimed his E "dodges the root, the bloom, AND the crouch" — the untargetable hop dodges damage, but what actually denies Pop Blossom in this kit is the grounding on Chum the Waters.
audit.why: Riot's text for Playful/Trickster gives untargetability, not grounding; grounding is on his R.
audit.corrected: Bodies replaced with Fizz-grounded content, and the denial attributed to the ability that actually carries it.

Crash timing: the crash is a timer you set — reset, plate, or roam, but never just because.

Worst wave: shoved to his tower with your E down and no clone banked, where Chum the Waters reaches from 1300 and grounds you on the way out. Crash timing: crash ahead of his roam timers and then follow him — his damage is map-wide, not in the duel.
